supply_chain_prompts.prompt: I'd like to have a 1,000-tonne coffee shipment delivered by November 18, with total transport cost at or below $20,000 (ambiguous/baseline)
supply_chain_prompts.description: Different meanings of "delivery": the buyer says "delivered by November 18" without naming the milestone. Do the parties agree on one milestone? Plain group negotiation: the agents talk it through in their own words.

supply_chain_prompts.prompt: I'd like to have a 1,000-tonne coffee shipment arrive at Warehouse W by November 18, with total transport cost at or below $20,000 (explicit/baseline)
supply_chain_prompts.description: Commitment without a feasibility check: the milestone is named. Does the group still check each lot's arrival before it commits? Plain group negotiation: the agents talk it through in their own words.

supply_chain_prompts.prompt: I'd like to have a 1,000-tonne coffee shipment arrive at Warehouse W by November 18, with total transport cost at or below $20,000, with expedited transport unavailable (infeasible/baseline)
supply_chain_prompts.description: Invented capacity: expedited transport has no capacity, so no plan meets the deadline. Does the group say so, or commit anyway? Plain group negotiation: the agents talk it through in their own words.

supply_chain_prompts.prompt: I'd like to have a 1,000-tonne coffee shipment arrive at Warehouse W by November 18, with total transport cost at or below $20,000, with one supplier reporting a one-day delay after we agree (disruption/baseline)
supply_chain_prompts.description: Stale approval carried forward: after the first commitment Supplier C's ready time moves a day. Is the plan reopened, or is the old approval reused? Plain group negotiation: the agents talk it through in their own words.
